key_insight: Albilich is a steerable, agentic framework that coordinates LLM reasoning, CAS, literature retrieval, and persistent state to make long-horizon mathematical research more reproducible and effective.
engineering_relevance: The paper shows how adding orchestration, verification, and memory layers can turn a general LLM into a practical research system for theorem proving and open-problem exploration.
method: Long-horizon proof-state management with persistent SQLite context
Advisor/verifier agents plus literature retrieval to steer and check proofs
CAS integration to reduce token use and improve symbolic reasoning
evidence_signal: On RealMath, Albilich solved 10/10 problems with CAS and 9/10 without CAS, and on Kourovka problems it produced a counterexample and a strengthened proof result.
watch_item: Results are benchmark- and problem-dependent, and the system’s reliability may hinge on verifier quality, advisor guidance, and careful CAS orchestration.
paper_title: Albilich: Steerable Proof-State Orchestration for LLM-Based Mathematical Research with CAS Integration
